description: Manually reviewed research summaries, not quotations. These studies do not validate this app or establish ideal sprint angles.

sources.title: Examination of 2D frontal and sagittal markerless motion capture: Implications for markerless applications
sources.population: Fifteen healthy adults walking; OpenPose compared with marker-based motion capture.
sources.summary: In sagittal recordings, occlusion substantially affected hip and knee estimates on the camera-far side. Visible-side measurements were more dependable in this setting.
sources.limitations: Walking and OpenPose results do not establish the accuracy of MediaPipe during sprinting. Visibility scores are not calibrated angle-error estimates.

sources.title: On the Importance of 'Front-Side Mechanics' in Athletics Sprinting
sources.population: Twenty-four competitive sprinters measured using high-speed three-dimensional motion capture.
sources.summary: Some front-side and back-side variables were associated with acceleration performance. The study did not find significant associations between those variables and maximum-velocity performance.
sources.limitations: Associations do not identify a universal ideal technique or show that changing an observed angle improves an individual athlete's speed. Sprint phase matters.

sources.title: 'Whip from the hip': thigh angular motion, ground contact mechanics, and running speed
sources.population: Forty participants with varied athletic backgrounds performing running trials across a range of speeds.
sources.summary: Thigh angular motion was associated with running speed across trials. The study supports examining thigh motion over a stride rather than judging a single pose in isolation.
sources.limitations: The app does not measure thigh angular velocity or ground reaction forces. An observed thigh-angle range cannot establish speed, force, or a causal performance deficit.

sources.title: VideoRun2D: Cost-Effective Markerless Motion Capture for Sprint Biomechanics
sources.population: Forty sprint recordings from five subjects; an adapted MoveNet system compared with manual annotation.
sources.summary: A specialized markerless sprint system was evaluated against manual trunk, hip and knee annotation. This illustrates the importance of checking a model against a defined reference task.
sources.limitations: The evaluated system and validation are different from this app's unmodified MediaPipe model. Its reported accuracy must not be claimed for Track Sprint AI.

sources.title: Unilateral and Bilateral Lower-Body Resistance Training Does not Transfer Equally to Sprint and Change of Direction Performance
sources.population: Thirty-three trained participants in a supervised resistance-training intervention.
sources.summary: Both squat and step-up training groups improved sprint performance, with an unclear difference between the groups for sprint outcomes.
sources.limitations: This does not show that a specific exercise will correct a video-derived joint angle. The app cannot infer a strength deficit or prescribe the study's program from footage.

sources.title: Kinematic stride cycle asymmetry is not associated with sprint performance and injury prevalence in athletic sprinters
sources.population: Competitive sprinters assessed during flying sprint trials.
sources.summary: The study did not find an association between measured stride-cycle asymmetry and sprint performance or injury prevalence in its sample.
sources.limitations: This does not prove that every asymmetry is harmless. A single oblique video cannot establish an anatomical imbalance, weakness, or injury risk.
